deliberate_differences: share_users_with_purchase is far higher than RetailRocket's: the RetailRocket warehouse is a sample of site visitors, most of whom never buy, while every simulated user is a returning customer observed for the whole window. The simulator keeps each binary 7-day target between 5 and 70 percent positive (tests/test_features.py, gate G1.4-06) so the models have both classes to learn.
buy_to_cart_ratio is higher because a simulated buy may skip the cart (a direct buy from the product page), while RetailRocket logs a transaction only after an add-to-cart event.

events_per_user_per_active_day is lower: RetailRocket's active days are dominated by a few heavy visitors, while each simulated shopper starts about one session a day of three to six screens. That keeps the default 1,000-user, 60-day run near 175,000 screens, which the extraction loader handles in about ten minutes.

median_events_per_session is higher and single_event_session_share lower: RetailRocket sessions are mostly one product view from a search result, while each simulated session has an intent family and a funnel, so the sessionizer and the comparison detector have bursts to recover (gate G1.4-05).
p90_events_per_session is lower: the simulator caps a session at 30 screens and exits the funnel after a buy, while RetailRocket has long browsing sessions by crawlers and heavy visitors.
